detail.title: Towards Virtual Twinning of Mines: Monitoring and Control of Underground Mine Air Quality by Utilising a Parametric 3D BIM Model
detail.abstract: Understanding air quality (AQ) in underground (UG) mine tunnels is vital for ensuring worker health and operational safety. Poor air conditions can pose serious health risks, and regulatory bodies require continuous monitoring and accurate documentation for compliance and inspection. Beyond regulatory needs, comprehensive AQ monitoring enables more effective mitigation of harmful compounds. This study explores the use of three-dimensional information modelling (IM) in UG tunnels to develop a parametric Mine Information Model (MIM). Drawing from Building Information Modelling (BIM) principles established in other sectors, the MIM serves as the basis for a Virtual Twin (VT) that supports AQ visualisation and management of dynamic datasets. The MIM integrates measured and simulated AQ parameters, aligning georeferenced and time-stamped data with a geometric model of the tunnel network. A completely new application of the Large Eddy Simulation (LES) method to simulate AQ in tunnels is also presented. These datasets are then visualised through a VT application, offering real-time environmental insight to support safer daily operations. The system also meets the air monitoring standards outlined in the European Union (EU) Directives on UG environments. Finally, the results and evaluations of a workshop organised among the mine staff to discuss the potential of the new methodology presented in this paper, i.e. information modelling in mining, will be presented.

Fundamentals of Operations Strategy: The Balanced Scorecard

Characteristics of a Balanced Scorecard

This note will explain the concept of a balanced scorecard—what it is, the different elements you would expect in one, and the considerations for its implementation.

A balanced scorecard is a performance-management tool that tracks the execution of activities along a number of dimensions. There are two important things to note. First, tracking the execution of activities is part of operations management, since the operations of a company broadly include all the activities the company performs. Second, a good scorecard uses a number of dimensions, not just one, to track these activities. Including many types of measurements is important because it creates a more complete view of the organization.

A few characteristics are common to all balanced scorecards. First, a balanced scorecard usually focuses on the strategic operations of the organization. Second, a balanced scorecard normally monitors and displays a careful selection of only a small number of metrics. It is not possible to consider monitoring hundreds or thousands of metrics, nor is this approach meaningful from a leadership decision-making perspective. Monitoring a small number of metrics, perhaps only three to five at the most, often makes the most sense. Third, a balanced scorecard normally contains a mix of both financial and nonfinancial metrics.

Every process has a bottleneck because every process has a limiting step. Product and Process: The Focused Factory

What Is a Focused Factory?

In this note, we will discuss the concept of a focused factory. This includes providing a definition of focused factories and exploring some real-world examples. A focused factory is not necessarily a physical factory that manufactures products. It is a term meant to capture the key operations strategy of a business unit, regardless of whether that business is manufacturing physical products or providing a service. Production is a general set of processes that use resources to transform inputs into outputs of higher value, whether those outputs are goods or services. With that in mind, let's look into the concept of a focused factory.

A focused factory is an operation that strives for a narrow range of processes, products, and intended customers. In other words, it's a specific set of processes designed to create only a few products, which are then intended for consumption by a specific customer group. It's the opposite of “trying to be everything to everyone.” This narrow range allows the operation to focus on doing few things very well, rather than doing many things in a mediocre manner.

What Are Factory Physics?

Factory physics does not actually involve physics. Rather, it is a term meant to capture a key trade-off in manufacturing operations. The word physics is meant to imply the sense of a universal rule that a manager should never forget. That rule has three components:

There is always variability.

The goal of a factory is to match production and demand with the lowest possible cost to produce the highest possible service.

In the context of variability, there are only three buffers available to match production and demand with low cost and high-quality service: inventory, capacity, and lead time.

Fundamentals of Process Improvement:A Brief Background on Process Improvement

A Brief Early History

In this note, we will provide a brief background on process-improvement and quality-management systems. Process improvement is a management philosophy that promotes the continuous improvement of products and services with a strong focus on the involvement of customers and employees. The field of quality management and our modern ideas about quality have emerged over the last 70 to 90 years. In the 1930s and 1940s, early “quality pioneers” W. Edwards Deming, Joseph Juran, and Philip B. Crosby outlined the principles of quality management in several publications.

After World War II, the Japanese (and particularly the executives at Toyota Motor Company) adopted these principles, and Japan held its first national quality award in 1951. However, US and European firms did not begin to implement quality as a branch of management science until the 1980s, when they began to suffer in global markets due to deficits in the relative quality of their products and services. To drive the new initiative home, the United States established the Malcolm Baldrige Quality Award in 1987. Today, quality management is imperative for any business. The bar continues to rise, as competition continues to provide products and services more quickly and cheaply and with more reliability, and to add value to customers in different ways.

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic delivered an unprecedented shock to business entry, with sharply contrasting effects on different types of startups. Using newly constructed administrative data from the Comprehensive Startup Panel covering the universe of U.S. startups, we provide the first official numbers of the pandemics impact on employer and nonemployer startup dynamics. Nonemployer startup formation declined substantially in 2020, while employer startups unexpectedly increased. Survival outcomes also diverged: nonemployer startup survival dropped markedly, whereas employer startup survival remained largely stable. These findings reveal a pronounced compositional shift and underscore the importance of designing policies tailored to nonemployer startups in economic crises.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of state-level Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Acts on advance notice and post-displacement labor market outcomes for U.S. workers from 1993 to 2019. State WARN adoption increases the likelihood of receiving 30+ days of notice by about 4 percentage points. Instrumental variables estimates, supplemented with local average response functions to address weak instruments, show that lengthy notice reduces immediate joblessness by 4 to 7 percentage points. The effects are most pronounced for low-skill workers. Longer term outcomes are less robust. The results indicate that enforceable mandates improve short run transitions, particularly for vulnerable workers.

detail.abstract:
This technical note is part of a set that focuses on the fundamentals of process improvement, including a brief background on process improvement, the basic elements of a process-improvement program, and common tools used in process improvement. While designed to be used together, these three notes can also be used as stand-alone documents to support particular learning objectives. The other notes in this set are “Fundamentals of Process Improvement: A Brief Background of Process Improvement” (UVA-OM-1666) and “Fundamentals of Process Improvement: Elements of Process-Improvement Systems” (UVA-OM-1667).These materials form one module in our collection of introductory operations management topics, and all are appropriate for an advanced undergraduate- or graduate-level introductory course on operations management. The complete list of the materials in this collection is available in the teaching materials included with this technical note.

Excerpt

Fundamentals of Process Improvement:Tools Used in Process Improvement

In this note, we will discuss some of the key tools used in continuous-improvement systems, also referred to as process-improvement systems. Process flow charts provide an understanding of the inputs and outputs of each process stage, and the motion of material throughout a process. They can help identify where breakdowns occur, how long activities take, and what is most important in terms of receiving items or information from one process stage and providing them to the next process stage.

Run charts are another important process-improvement tool. They help measure the performance of a metric over time, enabling new insights into it. A run chart might record the performance of a metric such as cost or quality over time and is read in a similar way to how one might read a cardiogram.

Scatter diagrams are simple graphs that plot one value against a second value. The first value might be an input to a process stage and the second might be the output. Scatter diagrams help us understand the relationship between two values. They also form the basis of regression analysis and provide insight into how correlated the values are to one another. In other technical notes in this series, we noted that you can perform regression analysis or fit a trend line to data to understand whether the first value is influencing the second one, or if the relationship is reversed.

detail.title: Hired Online: Exploring the Rise of Digital Hiring
detail.abstract: This summer internship project report, titled Hired Online: Exploring the Rise of Digital Hiring, conducted at Highland Agro Food Pvt. Ltd., examines the transformative role of digital media in modern talent acquisition. Highland Agro, a leading seafood processing and export company based in Khantapada, Balasore, Odisha, has embraced digital hiring to meet its growing manpower needs. Established in 2022, the company is part of the diversified Highland Group, with a strong focus on quality, sustainability, and innovation. The study investigates how digital platforms, content strategies, and employer branding influence recruitment effectiveness, while comparing digital methods to traditional hiring practices. The research pursued three primary objectives: (1) to explore the role of digital media in contemporary talent acquisition, (2) to analyze how content strategy, platform choice, and employer branding influence recruitment effectiveness, and (3) to evaluate the challenges and opportunities of digital hiring compared to traditional methods. A robust methodology was employed, involving a survey of 40 HR professionals and 100 students/job seekers, conducted over four weeks using Google Forms and structured interviews. Questionnaires included Likert scales, paired-comparison scales, and open-ended questions to capture quantitative and qualitative insights. Data was analyzed using Excel pivot tables, frequency distributions, and cross-tabulations to assess platform usage, candidate preferences, and HR perceptions. Key findings reveal that digital hiring offers significant advantages, including wider reach, cost efficiency, and faster hiring processes, with 72% of candidates recommending online channels for their accessibility. LinkedIn, Indeed, and Naukri emerged as dominant platforms, with 33% of candidates using multi-channel approaches. However, challenges such as digital fatigue, algorithmic biases, and limited digital literacy among rural job seekers persist. Notably, both HR professionals and candidates prioritize human touchpoints, with video interviews and LinkedIn sourcing yielding high satisfaction (75+ score). Highland Agro’s digital hiring efforts are progressing but face gaps in employer branding and platform optimization. Unlike competitors like Thai Union, which excels in digital recruitment through transparent, people-centric content, Highland Agro lacks a robust online presence, with no featured jobs or mission-driven content on platforms like LinkedIn. Recommendations include adopting a hybrid recruitment model, leveraging AI with regular bias audits, and enhancing employer branding through authentic content like “Day-in-the-Life” videos. Strategic partnerships, such as Highland’s MoU with Lulu Group in 2025, further amplify its market potential. By addressing these gaps, Highland Agro can strengthen its talent acquisition strategy and align with global digital hiring trends.

AI.tldr: 本研究探讨数字媒体在现代人才招聘中的变革作用，以Highland Agro食品公司为例，分析数字招聘平台、内容策略和雇主品牌对招聘效果的影响，并与传统招聘方法进行比较。
AI.research_question: 数字媒体在当代人才招聘中扮演什么角色？内容策略、平台选择和雇主品牌如何影响招聘效果？数字招聘相比传统方法面临哪些挑战和机遇？
AI.motivation: Highland Agro作为一家快速发展的海鲜加工出口公司，面临日益增长的人力需求，需要采用数字招聘来满足业务扩张需求。
AI.theoretical_framework: 数字招聘理论、雇主品牌理论、内容营销理论、招聘效果评估理论
AI.method: 混合研究方法：对40名HR专业人员和100名学生/求职者进行问卷调查和结构化访谈，使用Google Forms收集数据，采用李克特量表、配对比较量表和开放式问题，数据分析使用Excel数据透视表、频率分布和交叉表分析。
AI.findings: 数字招聘具有覆盖面广、成本效益高、招聘速度快等优势，72%的求职者推荐在线渠道；LinkedIn、Indeed和Naukri是主要平台，33%的求职者使用多渠道方法；但存在数字疲劳、算法偏见和农村求职者数字素养有限等挑战；视频面试和LinkedIn招聘满意度高（75+分）。
AI.theory_contributions: 丰富了数字招聘理论框架，提供了雇主品牌与招聘效果关系的实证证据，发展了混合招聘模型理论。
AI.practical_contributions: 为Highland Agro提供了具体的招聘策略改进建议，包括采用混合招聘模式、利用AI技术、加强雇主品牌建设，为企业应对数字招聘挑战提供了实践指导。

detail.abstract: How much of the most recent surge in inflation expectations, which began in March 2025, has been the result of the usual effect of abnormal price movements? How much is left unexplained and may signal a potential de-anchoring of inflation expectations? How do the most recent and the pandemic-era surges in expectations compare with the two surges in the Great Inflation episode of the 1970s?  This brief addresses those questions using data on inflation expectations from the University of Michigan Survey of Consumers and a simple regression model in which households form their inflation expectations based on their perception of movements in food and gas prices as well as broad-based inflation.

AI.tldr: 本文使用密歇根大学消费者调查数据和简单回归模型，分析了2025年3月以来通胀预期激增的原因，比较了疫情时期和1970年代大通胀时期的预期波动，评估了通胀预期脱锚风险。

AI.motivation: 理解近期通胀预期激增的原因，评估通胀预期脱锚风险，为货币政策提供参考。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于消费者形成通胀预期的行为模型，考虑食品和汽油价格变动感知以及广泛通胀的影响。
AI.method: 使用密歇根大学消费者调查数据，构建简单回归模型分析通胀预期的形成机制。
AI.findings: 部分通胀预期激增可由异常价格变动解释，但存在无法解释的部分可能暗示脱锚风险；不同时期的预期波动模式存在差异。
AI.theory_contributions: 深化了对通胀预期形成机制的理解，提供了评估通胀预期脱锚风险的实证框架。
